content.title: Friday Photography Club
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage:
Hi everyone,

This Friday, Photography Club will meet in Room 12, not in the library, because the library is closing early. We will start at 3:45 and finish at 5:00. Please bring one photo you would like to discuss. It can be on your phone or on paper. If you need to leave before 5:00, tell Ms Green before lunch on Friday. Students who are not club members can visit once, but they must email Ms Green by Thursday evening.

See you there!

content.title: Saturday Park Project: New Time
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage:
Hello volunteers,

Heavy rain is expected on Saturday morning, so our park clean-up will begin at 2:00 p.m. instead of 10:00 a.m. Please meet outside the sports centre, not at the park gate. A team leader will walk to the park with you. Bring water and wear old shoes. We will provide gloves, rubbish bags and all the other equipment. If you registered for the morning but cannot come in the afternoon, send us a message before 6:00 p.m. on Friday.

Thank you for helping!

content.title: A Change of Plan
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage: Last Sunday, Leo and Amir planned to spend the afternoon at the new skatepark. Their bus stopped two streets early because road workers had closed the main road. After they got off, Leo noticed that his backpack was still on the bus. His phone and wallet were inside it. The boys went into a nearby café and asked the owner for help. She called the bus company and gave them directions to its office. Twenty minutes later, the bus driver returned with the backpack. It was too late for the skatepark, so Leo and Amir walked by the river and took photos instead. Leo was disappointed at first, but he later said the afternoon was still fun.

options.text: A problem changed the boys' original plan, but the day ended well

Road workers showed the boys a better skatepark

What did Leo and Amir do after getting the backpack back?

options.text: They walked near the river and took pictures
They returned home on the same bus
They helped the workers open the road

False

content.title: Before the School Show
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage: Nina promised to help with the costumes before the school show on Friday. She wanted to arrive at four, but her alarm did not ring and she reached school thirty minutes late. In the hall, the actors were practising, but the costume boxes were locked in the main office. Nina looked for Mr Bell, the caretaker, and found him near the gym. He opened the office, and Nina carried the boxes to the hall with two friends. They quickly checked each costume and discovered that one jacket had no buttons. Nina used safety pins to fix it. The show started on time, and no one in the audience noticed the problem.

content.title: Finding the Outdoor Cinema
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage: On Saturday, Elena and Jo used a city app to find an outdoor cinema. The map showed an entrance beside the swimming pool, but the gate was locked. A small sign explained that the film had been relocated to the school hall because of strong wind. The girls followed orange arrows to the new place. Jo's phone had only two per cent battery, so she switched it off until they needed the map again. At the hall, volunteers gave them paper tickets. These allowed visitors to choose seats before entering. Elena kept hers in her jacket pocket because she did not want to lose it.

content.title: A Second-Hand Find
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage: Sam found some second-hand headphones at a weekend market. The seller said the left side was faulty: it played normally for a few minutes and then became silent. Sam still bought the headphones because the price was low and his cousin enjoys repairing electronics. At home, Sam showed them to her. She opened the left side and found a loose wire. After she connected it again, both sides worked perfectly. Sam thanked his cousin and offered to pay her, but she refused. She said fixing the headphones was good practice for her technology course.

content.title: The New Study Corner
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage: Our local youth centre has opened a study corner for students aged thirteen to seventeen. It is quieter than the main activity room and has six large desks, a printer and fast internet. Students can use it from Monday to Thursday between 3:30 and 7:00 p.m. There is no charge, but everyone must show a student card at reception. Drinks are allowed only in bottles with a lid, and food must stay in the café area. On Tuesdays, a university student is available to help with maths and science homework. The centre suggests arriving before five because the desks often fill quickly after that time.

content.title: A Weekend with the Parkers
content.source_note: Original unseen text created for Recovery Curriculum v2.
content.passage: Next month, Maya is staying with the Parker family during a school exchange in York. Their house is small but close to the city centre, so she will walk to school with their daughter, Ellie. Mr Parker works at a museum and usually returns home at six. Mrs Parker works from home and cooks dinner at about seven. The family has a friendly dog called Pepper, but it sleeps downstairs and never goes into the bedrooms. On Saturday, the Parkers plan to take Maya to the railway museum. If the weather is good on Sunday, they will have a picnic by the river; otherwise, they will visit an indoor market.
